title: Shubman Gill's Captaincy Record Trails Only Don Bradman Ahead of India's 600th Test
excerpt: India's 26-year-old skipper averages 82.76 in 15 innings as captain — second only to Sir Donald Bradman's 101.51 — as India prepare for the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15.
body:
• Shubman Gill's Test batting average as captain (82.76) ranks second all-time behind only Sir Donald Bradman (101.51) among skippers with at least 10 innings
  • Since taking over as India's Test captain in May 2025, Gill has scored 1,076 runs including six centuries and a career-best 269
  • India's first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle on August 15 will be the country's landmark 600th Test, falling on its 80th Independence Day
  • India sit fifth in the WTC 2025-27 standings and need strong results against Sri Lanka to stay in contention for the final

A Captaincy Defined by Runs

When Shubman Gill was named India's 37th Test captain on May 24, 2025, the appointment raised eyebrows. At 25, he was stepping into a role vacated by a generation of senior players, with a Test average hovering around 35. A year later, the numbers tell a different story.

https://x.com/Sports_NDTV/status/2088269105229136080

Gill has scored 1,076 runs in 15 innings as captain, with six centuries and a career-best 269. His captaincy average of 82.76 places him second on the all-time list of Test captains with at least 10 innings, trailing only Sir Donald Bradman's 101.51, according to CricViz data cited by NDTV Sports.

His pre-captaincy average across 59 innings stood at 35.05. The transformation has been sharp enough to demand attention.

The England Series That Changed Everything

Gill's breakout as captain came during the 2025 Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy in England. Over five Tests, he amassed 754 runs — the second-highest total by any captain in a single Test series, behind only Bradman's 810 in the 1936-37 Ashes, according to ESPN Cricinfo.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wd7Pwi7MZag

The runs came in clusters. Gill scored 147 in his captaincy debut at Headingley, then produced a monumental double of 269 and 161 at Edgbaston — the second-highest match aggregate in Test history. Under pressure in the fourth Test at Old Trafford, with India trailing by 311 runs and two wickets down for none, he battled a finger injury to grind out 103 off 238 balls.

"I am very comfortable with the role. I think the way we've been progressing in the past year has been very pleasing to see from my perspective."

— Shubman Gill, India captain

That fourth century made Gill only the third captain — after Bradman in 1947-48 and Sunil Gavaskar in 1978-79 — to score four hundreds in a single Test series. He was the first to achieve the feat in his debut series as captain.

The Sri Lanka Challenge

Gill leads India into the first Test against Sri Lanka at Galle's International Cricket Stadium starting Friday, August 15 — a date carrying double significance as India's 80th Independence Day and the country's 600th Test match. The second Test follows at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo from August 23-27.

The stakes are high in the World Test Championship standings. India sit fifth with a points percentage of 48.15 after four wins, four defeats, and a draw from nine matches. Sri Lanka are sixth at 44.44. A series sweep could significantly boost either team's path to the WTC final.

India will be without lead pacer Jasprit Bumrah, who was ruled out due to a left knee injury, with Jammu and Kashmir's Auqib Nabi earning a maiden call-up as his replacement. Ravindra Jadeja returns from a tennis elbow injury to strengthen the spin attack in subcontinental conditions. KL Rahul serves as vice-captain.

Approaching Another Milestone

In the current WTC 2025-27 cycle, Gill has scored 950 runs in eight Tests at an average of 79.16 with five centuries, making him the third-highest run-scorer in the cycle, according to LatestLY. He needs just 50 more runs in the first Test to become only the fourth Indian batter to complete 1,000 runs in a WTC cycle.

His overall Test record now stands at 2,969 runs in 41 matches at an average of 44.31 with 11 centuries.

Speaking to media ahead of the Galle Test, Gill said he felt the team was moving in the right direction under his leadership. For a captain whose bat has done most of the talking, the Sri Lanka series offers another chance to back those words with runs.
